figures.finding: St Kitts and Nevis has no permit or licence for child performers: the general Act reaches every employment of a child (under sixteen), so none may be employed under twelve (save for the parents at home or on their land), nor before school ends on a school day, before 6:00 or after 20:00, more than two hours on a school day or on a Sunday; the only allowance for performing is that the hour and two-hour limits do not stop a child taking part, unpaid, in an entertainment whose proceeds go to charity, education or anything but the promoters' profit. The Act draws no line between performing, writing or directing.

value.charityEntertainmentUnpaid: exempt from the 06:00-20:00 and two-hour school-day limits only

sources.said: no child shall be employed— (a) so long as he or she is under twelve years: provided however that such child may be employed by his or her parents or guardian in domestic work at home or in light agricultural or horticultural work on the land or garden of the parent or guardian; (b) before the close of school hours on any day on which he or she is required to attend school; (c) before six o’clock in the morning or after eight o’clock in the evening on any day; (d) for more than two hours on any day on which he or she is required to attend school; (e) for more than two hours on any Sunday;

(4) Nothing in paragraph (c) or paragraph (d) of Subsection (1), or in any regulations made under this section, shall prevent a child from taking part without fee or reward in an entertainment the net proceeds of which are devoted to any charitable or educational purpose or to any purpose other than the private profit of the promoters.

figures.finding: A person gains full age and legal capacity at eighteen and the Act governs every statute's and instrument's 'minor', 'infant' and 'full age'; no statute found provides for a court's or official's approval of a minor's engagement, or sets any share of a minor's earnings aside.

sources.said: A person shall attain full age and legal capacity on attaining the age of eighteen years.

figures.finding: No minor (a person below the age of legal capacity under the Federation's law or his domicile's, so under eighteen) may join in forming a company, become a member (save by inheriting shares) or be a director.

value.memberException: shares transmitted on the holder's death

figures.applies: St Kitts and Nevis (Companies Act, Cap. 21.03, ss 4, 28, 74).

sources.said: “minor” means a person who, under the law of the Federation or under the law of his or her domicile, has not reached the age of legal capacity; … Any number of persons (none of whom is a minor or an interdict or a bankrupt) associated for any lawful purpose may by subscribing their names to a memorandum of association form a company … A minor or an interdict may not become a member of a company unless the shares were transmitted to him or her on the death of the holder thereof. … (2) No person shall be a director who— (a) is a minor;
